notes: Corrected: *in* before *the land* moved from the verb's unit to אָרֶץ's. Rule 44's supplied-preposition sentence is conditioned on a bare direct object, and אָרֶץ after intransitive שָׁכַן is an accusative of place; rule 33's closing test — whether the English predicate admits another word before the complement — sends *in* to the noun, since the ASV writes *dwell upon* as well as *dwell in*.

The flagged three-morpheme unit לְ + עוֹלָם + בַּל → *never* is genuinely indivisible: no English word is spent on any one of the three, so rule 30's condition is met and rule 2 has no allocation to test. Head taken on the negative, with the temporal noun named as the competing head (rule 35).
The marginal *Or, earth* was read and set aside; the printed *land* governs.
